title: Valmiki takes in Sita
hookLine: a queen left alone at the forest's edge, and the poet who finds her
carry: the ramayana was born from compassion
tomorrow: why can't the mind let go?
last: THE SAME DAY, EACH ITS OWN MEANING.

lines: SITA ALONE AT THE FOREST'S EDGE.
THE STUDENTS RUN FOR THEIR TEACHER.
cards: A woman sits alone at the edge of a forest, crying. She is Sita, the queen of Ayodhya, and she's carrying a child.

Ram has sent her away because of what people in the city were saying, and the brother who drove her here has gone back. Young students from a nearby hermitage hear her and run to tell their teacher. He comes out to her.
He's Valmiki, the poet of the Ramayana, and he finds the heroine of his own story weeping at his door. Today, Punjab's last stop: a place tradition calls that door.

teach.b: In the last book of Valmiki's Ramayana, in paraphrase, Valmiki speaks gently to Sita. He tells her he knows she has done no wrong.
He brings her into his hermitage and gives her into the care of the women there, to be looked after like a daughter.
Her twin sons, Lava and Kusha, are born there, and Valmiki teaches them the Ramayana; in the story, they sing it, their own father's story, before Ram himself.

Why would the poet take her side when a whole city had turned on her? Go back to the start of his poem. In its first book, Valmiki watches a hunter shoot one of a pair of cranes as they call to each other.
The bird falls, and its mate cries over it.

teach.h: A CRANE FALLS; GRIEF BECOMES VERSE
teach.b: Grief pours out of Valmiki in a new kind of measured line, and he realizes he has made the first shloka, the verse: his shoka, grief, became shloka. Then Brahma tells him to use that verse to tell Ram's story.
The Ramayana is born from karuna, compassion, and tradition honors Valmiki as the adi kavi, the first poet, for exactly that. The poet who wept for a bird is the one who takes in a weeping queen.
And the place: tradition puts his hermitage at Ram Tirath, near Amritsar, with a temple and a sacred tank.

teach.h: THE FIRST POET TAKES HER IN.
teach.b: In Punjab, the Valmiki community honors him with special devotion as Bhagwan Valmiki, with processions on his birthday.

how: Pilgrims visit Ram Tirath near Amritsar, honored in tradition as Valmiki's hermitage, and Valmiki's birthday is kept in Punjab with processions and devotion.

games.q: you're Valmiki. your students tell you a pregnant woman is weeping at the forest's edge, and it's Sita, sent away from Ayodhya. what do you do?
o: send word to Ayodhya and wait.
bring her into the hermitage and care for her like a daughter.
write it down and stay inside.
games.why: Valmiki tells Sita he knows she's done no wrong, and gives her into the care of the hermitage women. her sons are born there.

practice: Think of a time when life turned hard and someone took you in: a friend's couch, a teacher's office, a grandparent's kitchen, a kind word at the right moment.
Let that person come to mind, feel what it was like to be sheltered, and for a few breaths simply wish them well; if you pray, hold them before God.
If life feels that hard right now, you don't have to carry it alone: in the US you can call or text 988, or call local emergency help.
